title: SIH summer internship program welcomes record number of high school students in 2026
text:
SIH summer internship program welcomes record number of high school students in 2026
Fifty-two Southern Illinois high school students participated in the 2026 SIH High School Summer Internship, which welcomed its largest class ever, according to an Aug. 12 announcement. The six-week program included students from 15 local high school districts who spent two to three days each week exploring healthcare careers and shadowing professionals across 19 departments at SIH Memorial Hospital of Carbondale, SIH Herrin Hospital, and SIH St. Joseph Memorial Hospital.
Jessica Vicente, Southern Illinois Healthcare Human Resources Recruiter and High School Summer Internship Coordinator, said the goal is to match students with departments that align with their interests while also exposing them to areas they may not have considered. “We try to see what interests students have, and then we try to put them in those departments that fulfill those interests,” Vicente said. “We also place them in other departments that they may not be aware of, just so they can see what else is out there.”
Interns observed real patient care and procedures but did not provide hands-on care. For some participants like Rachael Reams, a three-time intern and 2026 Herrin High School graduate, the experience shifted career plans: “I really want to go into labor and delivery so I can be a part of people’s special moments in life and just be there for them when they need comfort,” Reams said. She will begin the licensed practical nursing program at John A. Logan College this fall.
Amari Rose, another three-time intern from Sesser-Valier High School’s class of 2026, credited his experiences at SIH Outpatient Rehabilitation for helping him decide on a major in exercise science and sports performance as he pursues a career in physical therapy. Ella Zimmerle, an incoming senior at Carterville High School who returned for her second summer with SIH, found her interests changed after observing different specialties firsthand.
Zimmerle highlighted observing a hysterectomy performed by an all-female surgical team as especially memorable. Her mother Stacy Zimmerle noted how healthcare professionals answered Ella’s questions about education paths and careers: “I was very impressed with how Ella told me about her experiences.”
Southern Illinois Healthcare operates as a not-for-profit entity managing four hospitals along with more than 30 clinics and specialized centers; it employs over 4,000 people—making it the region's largest private employer—and supports community well-being through charity care programs while maintaining independent ownership status but engaging in collaborative affiliations. It has earned recognition for quality outcomes across several specialties including heart attack treatment and maternal health services, according to the official website.
